findings.reason: the node would hit its write fence on the file the field must come from, and the refusal reason — the whole point of the field — is unreachable from the grant as declared.
findings.text: §37's declared write paths (`reckon/crew/promotion.py` and the new test) do not include `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`, which is where the plan-review store is actually reached on the promotion path: `_plan_review_record_for_promoting_run` (`reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2394`) calls `plan_review.store_delivered_reviews` at `:2437`, and `reckon/crew/promotion.py` only imports that helper at `:2175` and assembles the receipt at `:1761`, carrying the ledger index append rather than anything from the plan-review store. §37's second done-when case requires the receipt to yield "the refusal's reason", which is produced by that call, so a node fenced to `promotion.py` cannot produce it without a second store call or reading the `store_error` field §23 landed on the sidecar; the plan's own §35 sets the precedent of deferring a write path until the cause is known, and here the path is knowable now.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `names_a_review_subject` (`reckon/crew/review.py:2019`) does accept a numeric version 0 and rejects an absent one, as §35 states; `join_admitted_plan_review` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:465`) and its admission caller `_join_admitted_plan_review` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1296`, called at `:1260` on every launched row) both resolve, and commit `02adfe851` exists with the message §35 describes; `_resolve_promotion_outcome` (`reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1411`), `review_delivery_refusal` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:482`), `_is_review_run` (`:45`, re-exported at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:199`) and `_index_append` (`reckon/ledger.py:2484`) all resolve; the four cited report directories exist and each carries a `report.md`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each unit's done-when is measurable: §35 requires a named layer, a responsible line and a reproducing command per instance, with logs under the report directory ending in `EXIT=`; §36 and §37 each carry four named cases, an explicit negative control (route the plan review back through `review_delivery_refusal`; drop the field), a base arm, and literal commands with `pytest -n 8`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §35 writes its report and reproduction logs under the run's report directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/a-plan-is-reviewed-before-it-is-built/`, which exists); §36 and §37 put every log under the run directory and use the run's scratch directory only for the git checkouts the two arms are cut from, not for evidence.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols the units name (`plan_review_store`) describe what they carry; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches code, and §35's census is cited by an investigation rather than embedded as a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §37 declares its write paths as `reckon/crew/promotion.py` and the new test, but the plan-review store call on the promotion path, and the refusal reason its done-when requires, live in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §35 has one deliverable (the investigation; the repair is explicitly deferred to its own section), §36 one (the default outcome distinguishes a plan review from a run review), §37 one (the `plan_review_store` receipt field).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `s35`, `s36` and `s37` each carry `data-links=""` and no `depends-on` is declared between them; none is needed, because §35 is read-only, §36 repairs the default outcome in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`, and §37 adds a receipt field in `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, and each stands alone. §36's suspicion that "the record promotion reads for a queue-launched run is the first suspect" cites §35 without depending on its conclusion.
